Mobility analysis · Las Vegas, NV

The Walk In
Routes to Allegiant Stadium

Anonymized device pings trace how fans actually move from event parking to kickoff — and back out again. Filters, map, and charts stay together in one frame the whole way down, so nothing resets while you explore.

Source: Azira Pinnacle pathing & visitation reports · anonymized, device-level GPS

01 — The full picture

Every qualifying trip, every lot

Each colored line is a real street segment, matched from raw GPS pings onto actual OpenStreetMap street geometry. Anything slower than the study window, or that never reached the stadium, was dropped as noise before this map was drawn.

Color and thickness show how many devices used that segment — the brighter red streets carry the most foot traffic. The animated flow direction shows whether a segment is carrying more people in (amber) or out (red) for your current filter.

03 — Locals vs. visitors

How locals walk in

Devices are classified by their Common Evening Location. Filtering to locals surfaces whether people who live in the Las Vegas metro favor different routes than out-of-town visitors.

Compare against another event

Load another game's dashboard_data.json (built by the same pipeline) to overlay its time-to-stadium distribution on the chart above.

Methodology. Trips are reconstructed from an Azira Pinnacle Pathing X export, with stadium arrival independently confirmed by a Pin report and spatially matched against the exact stadium footprint. A device only appears here if it pinged inside a mapped lot polygon and reached the stadium within the study's post-window; devices that never showed a confirmed arrival in that window were excluded as noise. Residency is derived from each device's Common Evening Location relative to the Las Vegas metro area. Lots with fewer than 38 qualifying devices are flagged low-confidence.

Street segments are matched offline, in the Python pipeline, against real OpenStreetMap street-centerline geometry (via --street-match) — not guessed live in the browser. Segment color and thickness show device volume; the animated flow direction shows whether a segment carries more inbound or outbound traffic for the current filter. "Devices per segment" and "entry points" both recompute live as you change the lot/residency filters, since the underlying data shipped to the browser is each trip's matched street sequence, not a single pre-baked total.
